what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Price it, then give it away to measure fit
sections.para: After asking whether people miss something, define a product, price it at what it is worth to you, deliver it at a cost that grows in steps, and offer it free to people who already know you. If they decline for lack of time or fit, the price is not the problem. Free still costs them attention.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: A stated price given free tests the product honestly
sections.para: Price first, since a price says what you think the thing is worth. Agentic delivery makes each extra customer cost a little more, not a lot. Offer it to early adopters without making them apply. Free is never free for them, so measure and cut their cost alongside policies created, customised and used.

sections.label: The step after "do they miss it"
sections.line: Define, price, deliver at flat marginal cost, then offer
sections.para: Something is not a product until it has a shape, a price and affordable delivery. RiskMandate's product is an Agent Behaviour Policy for one agent as an encrypted vault, priced at four tiers: £10, £50, £500 and £1,500. Agents provision and draft, a person corrects, so the twentieth customer costs about the same as the second.

sections.label: Free is not zero
sections.line: A free offer still costs recipients attention and time
sections.para: Giving something away asks people to read, think, decide, find twenty minutes for prompts and half an hour for a call, and fit it into their team. A price can even signal seriousness. The first measurement is that attrition: reply times, non-replies, abandoned prompts. Then cut it until the service costs both sides least.

sections.label: How to offer it
sections.line: Offer to early supporters directly; never make them apply
sections.para: "Apply for a chance" demands work before anything is in hand and inverts the relationship. Instead say there are twenty in the first round and ask yes or no. The first twenty should go to early adopters, power users and past customers, as thanks and as the best test group.

sections.label: What the programme is, as published
sections.line: The early access programme gives away the £500 tier
sections.para: The invite-only page went live on 30 September 2026 for people running an agent with real access. Each member gets a policy vault and is asked to say where it is wrong: twenty minutes of prompts, half an hour on a call. A person confirms within a working day and the vault follows within five.

sections.label: What brutal means
sections.line: If friendly users will not take it free, rethink
sections.para: If people take it, use it and ask for more, there is a product and the question becomes price. If they find no time, say it does not fit, or stall on the vault, there is no commercial product yet, and the drawing board is cheaper the sooner you reach it. Neither is a marketing problem.

sections.label: What we count
sections.line: Count policies created, customised, used, and the user's minutes
sections.para: The KPIs are Agent Behaviour Policies created, customised and used each day, and scenarios run. A policy created but never customised is a download; customised but unused is a document; commercial value lies in use. Added to these are the minutes each step costs the recipient and where they stopped.

sections.label: For the agents running this
sections.line: Agents running the programme: offer, time, count, set stops
sections.para: The first round goes only to the CRM list of early adopters, via a short yes-or-no message with an invitation code and no price. Record timings and drop-offs without message content, count the KPIs and corrections daily, treat every stop as a product finding, and set the stop rule before the first message.

sections.label: Why this is on a site about encrypted vaults
sections.line: The product, method and memory all live in vaults
sections.para: The product is a vault built with the machinery this site documents, and the agentic workflow makes giving twenty away affordable. The method matches the site's own. The site is also becoming memory: a future agent can read the chain from "do they miss it" to this article and the counts vault.
